newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BLACKBURN IN FIRST LEAGUE AWAY WIN OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLACKBURN IN FIRST LEAGUE AWAY WIN OF SEASON.

text.p: Blackburn Rovers recorded their first away English premier league victory of the season on Wednesday, beating Everton 2-0 to move out of the relegation zone.

Tim Sherwood put the 1995 champions ahead after 18 minutes, rounding off a neat move involving striker Chris Sutton and Kevin Gallacher with a left-foot strike that bounced in off Neville Southall's left-hand post.
Sutton secured the points with a 32nd minute goal -- his eighth of the season.
"We seem to have got things together," Sutton said. "But it's still going to be difficult to get away from the bottom of the table."

At the top, a solitary goal from Italian Roberto di Matteo was enough to give Chelsea a 1-0 win over front-runners Liverpool earlier in the day -- a result which cut the Merseysiders' lead to two points.

Chelsea, crushed 5-1 by Liverpool in the league at Anfield earlier this season, were forced to back-pedal for much of the first half as the visitors played their habitual patient passing game to near-perfection.

But di Matteo put Ruud Gullit's side ahead two minutes before halftime, capitalising on a mistake from Michael Thomas to run between the two centre-backs and score with a cool right-foot strike into the bottom left-hand corner of David James's net.

Chelsea kept their nerve after the interval and Mark Hughes almost put them 2-0 up when he crashed a shot against James's crossbar from a tight angle. In the end though, one goal was enough. Chelsea go sixth.

Arsenal beat Middlesbrough 2-0 to go back into second, two points behind Liverpool with a game in hand. Ian Wright scored Arsenal's second -- his 200th league goal -- after Dennis Bergkamp had sent the Gunners on their way with a crisp volley from 25 metres after 15 minutes.

Fabrizio Ravanelli earned a chance to bring Middlesbrough back into the match when he was scythed down by Patrick Vieira in the penalty area, but the former Juventus striker crashed his spot-kick against the crossbar.
With Blackburn winning, Middlesbrough now slip into the relegation zone.
John Hartson was sent off for the Londoners, for whom disciplinary problems are becoming a serious threat to their trophy ambitions.
Wright, now just 12 goals short of Arsenal's all-time scoring record, was playing his last game before starting a three-match suspension after being sent off at Nottingham Forest on December 21.
It was a disappointing day for Middlesbrough player-manager and former England captain Bryan Robson, who selected himself for the first time in over a year in response to a crippling injury crisis.
Robson, an inspirational midfielder with Manchester United in the 1980s, turns 40 later this month. Wednesday's match was his 568th league appearance.
While Robson was the oldest player on show in the New Year's Day premier league programme, Alan Shearer was the first to make his mark.

The England forward scored the first top flight goal of 1997, hammering home a volley from a corner after just four minutes against Leeds. He added a second in the 77th minute and Les Ferdinand scored a late third to ensure a 3-0 victory for Newcastle, a result which takes them into fourth.
Nottingham Forest moved off the bottom of the table with a 1-0 win at West Ham, pushing Southampton into bottom spot for the first time this season.
Champions Manchester United, five points behind Liverpool with two matches in hand, were playing Aston Villa later in the day.
